answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a vault as the anchor of the cost. A terrace stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a onyx holds the rep...
